negative_index.php demonstrates first-match, last-match, and null-on-out-of-bounds

summary: Created examples/02-selectors/attribute_selectors.php: demonstrates [attr^=val], [attr$=val], [attr*=val], [!attr], and comma-grouped selectors with a single rich fixture.

Created examples/02-selectors/negative_index.php: demonstrates idx=0 (first), idx=-1 (last), idx=-2 (second-to-last), positive idx (nth), out-of-bounds→null, selector-with-no-match→null, and idx=null (full array). The find() negative-index implementation (count+idx) was verified in source.
Created examples/02-selectors/text_nodes.php: demonstrates find('text') on document and scoped to a single element, and text node manipulation via $node->innertext = uppercased value.
All files: php -l clean, no HTML tags in output (grep confirmed 0 matches), no HTTP requests, _bootstrap.php included, clear() called after each fixture.

comments.note: text_nodes.php: find('text') returns ALL text nodes in the subtree including whitespace-only nodes between tags. The example defensively filters with trim() !== '' before printing, which keeps output readable. QA might want to verify this filtering is the expected pattern for the docs.

summary: All 6 acceptance criteria verified and passing.
AC1: php -l passes on all 3 files.

AC2: attribute_selectors.php delivers all five variants — [^=] (secure links), [$=] (PDF links), [*=] (btn class), [!disabled] (absent attribute), and comma-grouped selectors. Output is non-empty and correct for each section.

AC3: negative_index.php correctly demonstrates idx=0 (first), idx=-1 (last), idx=-2 (second-to-last), positive idx (nth), out-of-bounds idx=100 → null, no-match selector → null, and full-array (no index arg). First/last/null-on-out-of-bounds AC3 requirement fully met.

AC4: text_nodes.php demonstrates find('text') on document (11 total nodes, 7 non-whitespace displayed), text node manipulation via innertext uppercasing, and scoped find('text') on a single element — all sections produce correct CLI output.
AC5: No network-making functions found. All examples use str_get_html() with inline heredoc fixtures only.
AC6: All 3 files include require __DIR__ . '/../_bootstrap.php' at line 5 and produce section()-formatted CLI output.
Regression: 278/278 PHPUnit tests pass (no new tests required for example files).

comments.note: text_nodes.php uses trim() !== '' to filter whitespace-only text nodes before display. This is the correct approach and keeps output readable, but the example does not explain why — a brief inline comment noting 'text nodes between tags are often whitespace-only' would help readers understand the defence.

attribute_selectors.php: the comma-group section demonstrates 'a[href^=http], button' which mixes two different element types in one selector. This works, but the section header says only 'a[href^=http], button' — clarifying this produces elements of different types (a and button) in one pass would be more pedagogically explicit.
No observations requiring code changes — all files are clean and consistent with the established patterns from WP-002.

summary: All three WP-003 files pass code review across all four dimensions.
attribute_selectors.php: single shared fixture covering all five selector variants cleanly; comma-group output shows element tags making mixed types self-evident at runtime.
negative_index.php: excellent null-guard pattern for out-of-bounds and no-match cases demonstrated explicitly — a strong teaching pattern.
text_nodes.php: three-fixture structure isolates each concept clearly; whitespace-only filtering is correct and now annotated. No Blocking issues.

comments.note: text_nodes.php: added inline comment `// text nodes between HTML tags are often whitespace-only; skip them` on the trim-filter guard. Both QA and the Developer flagged this filter as helpful but unexplained; a reader learning from this file now understands why the guard exists.

negative_index.php is exemplary in its null-guard pattern for the out-of-bounds and no-match cases (explicit null check before property access). This is the defensive idiom readers should internalize — consider cross-referencing it from api-surface.md or the docs README as the canonical pattern for indexed find() calls.
No observations requiring code changes — all three files are clean, consistent, and follow established WP-002 patterns perfectly.
